text: Chapter 6 shifts from tools to content: the specific reports a working consultant produces every month, starting with the two most fundamental financial statements.

The Income Statement reports performance over a period, did this business make money this month. Revenue, minus Cost of Goods Sold, gives Gross Margin, a formula row. Minus Operating Expenses gives Net Income, the final formula row. Columns typically compare periods, this month versus last month or budget.

The Balance Sheet reports position at a single point in time, not what happened, but where things stand right now. It follows the accounting equation, Assets equal Liabilities plus Equity. Assets are what the business owns, Liabilities are what it owes, Equity is the owners' residual claim, including retained earnings.

The two statements connect. Net Income from the Income Statement flows into Retained Earnings on the Balance Sheet's Equity section, period after period. A Balance Sheet that doesn't tie to accumulated Net Income across prior periods is a sign something in close needs investigation, not two unrelated reports that happen to disagree.

Experienced consultants check three things fast: does the point of view match, does the Balance Sheet actually balance to the cent, and does retained earnings reconcile period to period. Up next, lesson twenty-five: Trial Balance and Account Analysis reports, the detail behind these two statements.
